statusNote: Founder review pending: each expectation and its reason are a proposal until Vieri confirms or edits them with the rubric in next-action-rubric.json.

conventions.times: Day offsets from now; negative is the past. Now is 09:00 UTC, and the day is the UTC day.
conventions.goal: Defaults: level task, status active, health on_track, score 0, created -3, never activated after creation, no progress, no dependencies, sort 0, no deadline, escalation none.
conventions.work: Defaults: mode manual, no goal, created -0.125 (06:00 today), no blocker, no check, not closed in Tasks, no workflow. A waitpoint blocker is [kind, reason, who resumes it: you (default), timer or outside]. closed is [completed or failed, day] for an item closed in Tasks.
conventions.commitment: Defaults: status pending, no due date.
conventions.done: Titles of commitments finished on a given day, besides finished work items.

scenarios.situation: This week's invoice reminders ran and finished. Pricing work is also waiting.
scenarios.why: A finished run is not progress until you confirm it. Checking is quick and closes the loop before more work starts.

scenarios.situation: The reminder run is paused, waiting for approval to send.
scenarios.why: Accepted work is stuck on an answer only the founder can give.

scenarios.situation: The reminder run failed and nobody has looked at it.
scenarios.why: A failure nobody has looked at hides whether anything was sent; settle it before planning more.

scenarios.situation: Accepted follow-up work runs a workflow whose Gmail account is disconnected. Another goal has a startable step.
scenarios.why: Running it would fail. Reconnecting the account unblocks work already accepted, which comes before starting something new.

scenarios.situation: This morning's plan proposed two items, one for a goal due in two days.
scenarios.why: Proposals need a yes or no before they are work; the one serving the sooner deadline first.

scenarios.situation: Accepted reminder work is ready. Another goal has no work yet.
scenarios.why: Finish what was already accepted before adding new work.

scenarios.situation: Reminder work was checked done two days ago, but the goal is still open. A pricing goal has a startable step.
scenarios.why: Sending the reminders again would duplicate finished work. Recording whether the goal is done adds no work and comes before starting the pricing step.

scenarios.situation: Reminder work was checked done two days ago, the goal is still open, and nothing else is active.
scenarios.why: The goal looks done; recording that is the next action, not repeating the work.

scenarios.situation: Every task under the invoice key result is complete, but the key result is still open.
scenarios.why: The steps are done; whether the key result is met is a decision, not another task.

scenarios.situation: A newsletter goal has had no progress or work for six weeks.
scenarios.why: Six idle weeks suggest the goal no longer matters as stated; ask before adding work to it.

scenarios.situation: The newsletter goal is stale; a pricing goal created this week has a startable step.
scenarios.why: Live work comes before reviewing a stale goal, and the stale goal never gets a fresh task by default.

scenarios.situation: The founder already committed to calling Ana about invoice 1042.
scenarios.why: Recommending the call again would duplicate an existing commitment.

scenarios.situation: Sending the new price list depends on approving the new prices, which is not done.

goals.title: Send the new price list to customers

scenarios.why: Blocked work is not executable; the dependency is the useful next step.

scenarios.situation: Accepted work on the price-list goal is ready, but that goal waits on approving the new prices.

goals.title: Send the new price list to customers

scenarios.why: Accepted is not unblocked: the work waits on its goal's dependency, which is the useful step.

scenarios.situation: A proposal to draft the partner agreement exists without a goal link; the matching goal has no work of its own.
scenarios.why: The existing proposal is the step; deciding it beats creating a second copy.

scenarios.situation: The only key result belongs to a paused objective.
scenarios.why: Paused means not now. With nothing else live, the honest answer is that nothing is waiting.

scenarios.situation: Five items are running, the daily limit, and a new step is available.
scenarios.why: Adding a sixth item to a full day is noise; the answer is to let current work finish.

scenarios.situation: The day is full, but one item finished and needs checking.
scenarios.why: Checking reduces the load instead of adding to it.

scenarios.situation: The objective has no tasks under it yet.
scenarios.why: Any concrete step would be invented; asking for the first step is more useful.

scenarios.situation: The last reminder attempt failed its check: three reminders bounced.
scenarios.why: Repeating a failed attempt blindly wastes effort; the founder decides whether to retry or change the approach.

scenarios.situation: Two goals with no deadlines, the same health and no order between them each have a startable step.
scenarios.why: Nothing in the data separates them; picking one would be a coin flip presented as advice.

scenarios.situation: Two startable goals; one is due in three days.
scenarios.why: The deadline is the evidence that separates them.

scenarios.situation: Every goal is complete and the last item is still running.
scenarios.why: There is nothing to add; inventing work would be noise.

scenarios.situation: Proposals from earlier mornings were never decided and one was rejected. This morning a run finished.
scenarios.why: Undecided proposals from earlier days are stale, as the Today view treats them; they neither crowd out new work nor fill the day.

scenarios.situation: Reminder work was checked done two days ago. This morning's fallback plan proposed working on the same goal again.
scenarios.why: Accepting the proposal would repeat finished work. Whether the goal is done is the real decision.

scenarios.situation: Emailing the price list, due in three days, sits under a milestone that waits on approving the new prices.

goals.title: Review the price sheet with Ana
Email the price list to customers

scenarios.why: A step inherits its parent's dependencies. The email cannot go out before the prices are approved, so the approval's step comes first despite the deadline.

scenarios.situation: Reminder work was checked done ten days ago; the goal is still open and nothing else is active.
scenarios.why: Finished work stays finished; a week later it must not come back as a new step.

scenarios.situation: A commitment with the goal's exact title was finished three days ago, without a link to the goal.
scenarios.why: The call already happened; the open goal needs recording, not another call.

scenarios.situation: Accepted reminder work was marked done in Tasks yesterday, without a result check.
scenarios.why: Marking it done in Tasks settles it as surely as a check; asking to do it again would be wrong.

scenarios.situation: A follow-up workflow is in its three-day wait. A pricing goal has a startable step.
scenarios.why: The wait ends by itself, so there is nothing to answer. It still counts toward the day.

scenarios.situation: A run waits for approval to send, but its goal was paused yesterday.
scenarios.why: Approving would send email for a goal you paused. It waits until you resume the goal.

scenarios.situation: A task under a key result due tomorrow, and a standalone task due in five days.
scenarios.why: A step inherits its parent's deadline; tomorrow's key result comes before a task due in five days.

scenarios.situation: Five items are running, the daily limit. A goal's work was checked done yesterday, and another goal has a startable step.
scenarios.why: Recording a finished goal adds no work, so a full day does not hide it; only the new step waits.

scenarios.situation: The launch email waits on a beta goal that was killed.
scenarios.why: A dependency that can never finish holds the goal forever; fixing it is the useful step, not reporting that nothing is waiting.
